questions.question:
In the adjoining figure line l is parallel to line m. What is the value of (x + 2y) ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/905c2a270ecc9e29bc4cc0942201541f2d5e6ffded406685ccf504d4f877d95c.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify that **line l** and **line m** are **parallel**, making **x** and **y** co-interior angles.

The sum of **co-interior angles** is always **180°**, so **x + y = 180°**.

The expression **(x + 2y)** can be rewritten as **(x + y) + y**.

From the geometric figure, the obtuse angle **y** is **135°**, which means **x = 45°**.

⇒ **(x + 2y) = 180° + 135° = 315°**.

**∴ The correct answer is 315°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Line **l || m**.

⇒ Angle **x** and angle **y** are **interior angles** on the same side of the **transversal**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Sum of **co-interior angles** = **180°**.

⇒ **Linear Pair** property: Sum of angles on a straight line = **180°**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb6df9dee73600e7e976b5de82ac218cd1bc9d20a3a619d5ebb5302638e9bf98.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since **l || m**, the **co-interior angles** **x** and **y** satisfy the condition: **x + y = 180°**.

⇒ From the given figure, the value of the **obtuse angle** **y** is observed to be **135°**.

⇒ To find **x**: **x = 180° − 135° = 45°**.

⇒ Now, calculate the required value: **(x + 2y)**.

⇒ **(x + 2y) = 45° + 2(135°)**.

⇒ **(x + 2y) = 45° + 270°**.

⇒ **(x + 2y) = 315°**.

**∴ The correct answer is 315°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the angles in matching corners are equal.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between parallel lines on opposite sides of a transversal are equal (Z-pattern).

Consecutive Interior Angles

Also known as co-interior angles, these are located between the parallel lines on the same side and sum to 180°.</p

questions.question: If two interior angles on the same side of a transversal intersecting two parallel lines are in the ratio 2 : 3, then the greater of the two angles is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **consecutive interior angles** between parallel lines is 180°.

Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 = 5 units.

5 units → 180°

1 unit → 180° ÷ 5 = 36°

Greater angle = 3 units = 3 × 36° = 108°.

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **interior angles** on the same side = 2 : 3.

**Formula Used:**

When two **parallel lines** are cut by a **transversal**, the sum of the interior angles on the same side is always 180° (supplementary angles).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f76d37fca03371db8985b1bcfd7db33b169fa187b2e1026a6ec36cb432856002.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two interior angles be 2x and 3x.

⇒ According to the property of **parallel lines**:

⇒ 2x + 3x = 180°

⇒ 5x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 5

⇒ x = 36°

⇒ Smaller angle = 2x = 2 × 36° = 72°

⇒ Greater angle = 3x = 3 × 36° = 108°

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Interior Angles

These are the pairs of angles on one side of the transversal and between the two lines. If the lines are parallel, they are **supplementary** (sum = 180°).

Alternate Interior Angles

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the **alternate interior angles** are equal in measure.

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. If the lines are parallel, these angles are **equal**.</p

questions.question: Two angles are complementary. The larger angle is 6° less than five times the measure of the smaller angle. What is the measure of the larger angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of **complementary angles** = 90°.

Let the **smaller angle** be 1 unit.

Then the **larger angle** = 5 units − 6°.

Sum: 1 unit + 5 units − 6° = 90° ⇒ 6 units = 96°.

⇒ 1 unit = 16° (smaller angle).

**Larger angle** = 90° − 16° = 74°.

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ The two angles are **complementary** (sum = 90°).

⇒ The **larger angle** is 6° less than 5 times the **smaller angle**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Sum of complementary angles: α + β = 90°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa26acdf097a7c6ea6336856c5df6eb68ec0fe2d0e1c65eafd825a0e150ecaf5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the measure of the **smaller angle** be x.

⇒ According to the question, the **larger angle** = 5x − 6.

⇒ x + (5x − 6) = 90

⇒ 6x − 6 = 90

⇒ 6x = 90 + 6

⇒ 6x = 96

⇒ x = 96 ÷ 6 = 16°

⇒ **Larger angle** = 5(16) − 6 = 80 − 6 = 74°.

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are said to be supplementary if the sum of their measures is exactly 180°.

Linear Pair of Angles

A pair of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines, where the sum of the angles is always 180°.

Adjacent Angles

Angles that share a common vertex and a common side but do not overlap.</p

questions.question:
When there are two parallel lines cut by a transversal, which of the following is true?

a) Corresponding angles are equal.

b) Alternate interior angles are supplementary.

c) Consecutive angles on the same side of the transversal are equal.

d) Alternate interior angles are equal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **geometry**, when two **parallel lines** are intersected by a **transversal**:

• **Corresponding angles** are always **equal** (Statement a is true).

• **Alternate interior angles** are always **equal** (Statement d is true, statement b is false).

• **Consecutive (co-interior) angles** sum to 180°, meaning they are **supplementary**, not equal (Statement c is false).

**∴ The correct answer is a and d .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two parallel lines (m || n) and a transversal line (t).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/237ad79d0ea437bd360bb8c22a6cbd7af855e3a9118f9550b59c60ec1dfb2f52.png] 

Analyzing the pairs of angles from the diagram:

⇒ **Corresponding Angles:** Pairs like ∠1 and ∠5 or ∠2 and ∠6 are in the same relative position. By the **Corresponding Angles Postulate**, ∠1 = ∠5. Hence, statement (a) is **true**.

⇒ **Alternate Interior Angles:** Pairs like ∠4 and ∠6 or ∠3 and ∠5 are on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines. By the **Alternate Interior Angles Theorem**, ∠4 = ∠6. Hence, statement (d) is **true**.

⇒ **Alternate Interior Angles (Supplementary check):** Since ∠4 = ∠6, they are only supplementary if they are both 90°. In general, they are **equal**, not supplementary. Hence, statement (b) is **false**.

⇒ **Consecutive Interior Angles:** Pairs like ∠4 and ∠5 are on the same side. By the **Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem**, ∠4 + ∠5 = 180°. They are **supplementary**, not necessarily equal. Hence, statement (c) is **false**.

**∴ The correct answer is a and d .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other at the vertex are always equal (e.g., ∠1 = ∠3 and ∠2 = ∠4).

Linear Pair of Angles

Angles that lie on a straight line and share a common arm are supplementary, meaning their sum is 180° (e.g., ∠1 + ∠2 = 180°).

Alternate Exterior Angles

Pairs of angles on opposite sides of the transversal and outside the parallel lines (e.g., ∠1 and ∠7) are always equal.</p

questions.question: If a regular polygon has 20 diagonals, then the number of sides of this polygon is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The number of **diagonals** in a polygon with n sides is given by n(n − 3) ÷ 2.

Test the given options to find which value of n results in 20 diagonals:

For n = 8: 8 × (8 − 3) ÷ 2 = 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20.

This matches the given condition, so the **number of sides** must be 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **diagonals** in a **regular polygon** = 20

**Formula Used:**

Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2, where n is the **number of sides**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9497ac5e2a7bc10765088134006450d29667e23329e0bcd83471d1a626167f3a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 20

⇒ n(n − 3) = 20 × 2

⇒ n² − 3n = 40

⇒ n² − 3n − 40 = 0

⇒ n² − 8n + 5n − 40 = 0

⇒ n(n − 8) + 5(n − 8) = 0

⇒ (n − 8)(n + 5) = 0

⇒ n = 8 or n = −5

Since the **number of sides** must be a **positive integer**, we take n = 8.

Therefore, **Option 3** is the correct one.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon, the sum of all exterior angles is always 360°.

Individual Angle of a Regular Polygon

Each interior angle = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n and each exterior angle = 360° ÷ n.

Diagonal Formula Derivation

From n vertices, nC2 lines can be drawn. Subtracting n sides gives n(n−1)/2 − n = n(n−3)/2 diagonals.</p

questions.question: If a regular polygon has 35 diagonals, then the sum of its interior angles is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Number of **diagonals** = n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 35

⇒ n(n − 3) = 70

⇒ 10 × (10 − 3) = 70, so **n = 10** sides.

**Sum of interior angles** = (n − 2) × 180°

⇒ (10 − 2) × 180° = 8 × 180° = 1440°.

**∴ The correct answer is 1440°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number of diagonals of a regular polygon = 35.

**Formula Used:**

1. Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

2. Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°

where **n** represents the number of sides of the polygon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0db266582fd37e57cd8e37f4d2e8de823d3a33db37c442627386f535aabfa3d6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 35

⇒ n² − 3n = 70

⇒ n² − 3n − 70 = 0

⇒ n² − 10n + 7n − 70 = 0

⇒ n(n − 10) + 7(n − 10) = 0

⇒ (n − 10)(n + 7) = 0

⇒ n = 10 (since number of sides cannot be negative, n = −7 is rejected).

Now, calculate the **sum of interior angles**:

⇒ Sum = (10 − 2) × 180°

⇒ Sum = 8 × 180° = 1440°.

**∴ The correct answer is 1440°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Each Interior Angle

For a regular polygon, each interior angle is given by [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon is always 360°.

Each Exterior Angle

For a regular polygon, each exterior angle is 360° ÷ n. Also, Interior Angle + Exterior Angle = 180°.</p

questions.question: If a regular polygon has 65 diagonals, then the number of sides this polygon has is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **regular polygon** with **n sides**, the number of **diagonals** is given by the formula: **n(n − 3) ÷ 2**.

⇒ n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 65

⇒ n(n − 3) = 130

We need to find two factors of 130 that differ by 3.

⇒ 130 = 13 × 10

Comparing n(n − 3) with 13(10), we get **n = 13**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **diagonals** in the **regular polygon** = 65.

**Formula Used:**

Number of diagonals in an **n-sided polygon** = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b0417aa313b8cda1e3fd9d8bcdd2e8e685200a9377021a7cb40871fe4550e37.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 65 = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

⇒ 130 = n² − 3n

⇒ n² − 3n − 130 = 0

To solve this **quadratic equation**, we split the middle term:

⇒ n² − 13n + 10n − 130 = 0

⇒ n(n − 13) + 10(n − 13) = 0

⇒ (n − 13)(n + 10) = 0

Possible values for n are:

⇒ n = 13 or n = −10

Since the **number of sides** (n) cannot be negative, we take n = 13.

The polygon is a **Tridecagon** (a 13-sided polygon).

**∴ The correct answer is 13 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal Formula Derivation

The number of ways to pick 2 vertices from n is ⁿC₂. Subtracting the n outer sides gives the diagonals: [n(n − 1) ÷ 2] − n = n(n − 3) ÷ 2.

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all **interior angles** of an n-sided polygon is (n − 2) × 180°. For a tridecagon, it is 11 × 180° = 1980°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any **convex polygon**, the sum of all **exterior angles** is always constant and equal to 360°.

Each Interior Angle of a Regular Polygon

Each interior angle of a **regular polygon** is calculated as [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n.</p

questions.question: In a quadrilateral PQRS, if the sum of measures of angles ∠Q and ∠S is 150° while the measures of angles ∠P and ∠R are in ratio 4 : 3, then the measure of ∠R will be
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of all internal angles in a **quadrilateral** = 360°.

Given ∠Q + ∠S = 150°, then ∠P + ∠R = 360° − 150° = 210°.

The ratio of ∠P : ∠R = 4 : 3. Sum of ratio parts = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

7 units = 210° ⇒ 1 unit = 30°.

∴ ∠R = 3 units = 3 × 30° = 90°.

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of angles ∠Q and ∠S = 150°

Ratio of ∠P and ∠R = 4 : 3

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of a **quadrilateral** = 360°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52ebaca184c0e5bebc6da26ff310789cd1fcb10611da0b7f7a7673a9daa9c00a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ (∠P + ∠R) + (∠Q + ∠S) = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠R + 150° = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠R = 360° − 150° = 210°

Let ∠P = 4x and ∠R = 3x

⇒ 4x + 3x = 210°

⇒ 7x = 210°

⇒ x = 210° ÷ 7 = 30°

⇒ ∠R = 3x = 3 × 30° = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of interior angles of a Polygon

The sum of interior angles of any polygon with n sides is given by the formula (n − 2) × 180°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is always 180°. (∠P + ∠R = 180° and ∠Q + ∠S = 180°).

Angle Sum Property of Triangle

The sum of all three interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.</p

questions.question: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 7 : 10. Find the difference between the greatest and the smallest angles of the quadrilateral.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **ratio parts** = 2 + 5 + 7 + 10 = 24 units.

Total **internal angles** of a quadrilateral = 360°.

⇒ 24 units = 360° ⇒ 1 unit = 15°.

**Difference** between greatest (10) and smallest (2) parts = 10 − 2 = 8 units.

⇒ Difference = 8 × 15° = 120°.

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of angles = 2 : 5 : 7 : 10.

**Formula Used:** Sum of all interior angles of a **quadrilateral** is always 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61b2a819f1131ba03ae6cc2fbb990d82a34444d7a779435098af6853e38d7178.png] 

⇒ Let the four angles be 2x, 5x, 7x, and 10x respectively.

⇒ 2x + 5x + 7x + 10x = 360°

⇒ 24x = 360°

⇒ x = 360° ÷ 24

⇒ x = 15°

⇒ **Smallest angle** = 2x = 2 × 15° = 30°

⇒ **Greatest angle** = 10x = 10 × 15° = 150°

⇒ **Difference** = 150° − 30° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property of Polygons

The sum of internal angles of any polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of **opposite angles** is always 180°.

Exterior Angle Sum

The sum of all **exterior angles** of any convex quadrilateral (or any polygon) is always 360°.</p

questions.question: If, in the quadrilateral JKLM, the measures of the angles J, K, L, and M are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 : 6, then the quadrilateral is a:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio** of angles J : K : L : M is 2 : 3 : 5 : 6.

Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 16 parts.

Since the total sum of angles is 360°, then 16 parts = 360° → 1 part = 22.5°.

Check **co-interior angle sums**: J + M = (2 + 6) × 22.5° = 180° and K + L = (3 + 5) × 22.5° = 180°.

When co-interior angles sum to 180°, the sides **JK and ML** are **parallel**.

A quadrilateral with only one pair of **parallel sides** is defined as a **Trapezium**.

**∴ The correct answer is Trapezium.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The measures of the angles J, K, L, and M of **quadrilateral JKLM** are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 : 6.

**Formula Used:** Sum of all interior angles of a **quadrilateral** = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0049cada488f17ba3d9019f52a75403de5f4fa63c5bc8a6bc3f14ee00eb1ec27.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the angles be 2x, 3x, 5x, and 6x.

⇒ 2x + 3x + 5x + 6x = 360°

⇒ 16x = 360°

⇒ x = 22.5°

⇒ Angle J = 2 × 22.5° = 45°

⇒ Angle K = 3 × 22.5° = 67.5°

⇒ Angle L = 5 × 22.5° = 112.5°

⇒ Angle M = 6 × 22.5° = 135°

⇒ Observe the sum of adjacent angles: J + M = 45° + 135° = 180°.

⇒ Similarly, K + L = 67.5° + 112.5° = 180°.

⇒ Since the sum of **co-interior angles** is 180°, the side **JK is parallel to ML**.

⇒ Because only one pair of opposite sides is parallel and the other sides (JM and KL) are not parallel (J + K ≠ 180°), the quadrilateral is a **Trapezium**.

**∴ The correct answer is Trapezium.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Trapezium

A **Trapezium** is a quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides. The angles on the same side of the non-parallel legs are **supplementary** (sum to 180°).

Sum of Angles in Polygons

For any polygon with n sides, the sum of internal angles is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n=4), the sum is 2 × 180° = 360°.

Parallel Line Properties

If a transversal intersects two lines such that the sum of **co-interior angles** is 180°, then the two lines are **parallel**.</p

questions.question: In two triangles ABC and DEF, if overline{AB} = overline{EF} , overline{BC} = overline{DF} and overline{CA} = overline{DE} , then:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the correct **congruence** relation, identify the **corresponding vertices** by looking at the shared sides.

Common vertex in AB and BC is **B**; common vertex in EF and DF is **F** ⇒ B corresponds to F.

Common vertex in BC and CA is **C**; common vertex in DF and DE is **D** ⇒ C corresponds to D.

Common vertex in CA and AB is **A**; common vertex in DE and EF is **E** ⇒ A corresponds to E.

Mapping vertices: C → D, B → F, A → E.

Arranging them in order gives **ΔCBA ≅ ΔDFE**.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔCBA ≅ ΔDFE.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In **ΔABC** and **ΔDEF**:

AB = EF

BC = DF

CA = DE

**Formula Used:**

**SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence Rule:** Two triangles are congruent if all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other triangle. The **order of vertices** must match the **equal sides**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5ff9f1f554e5d1e59117137b8c9c97dc1508a3fbb75a3ec1d26a290a31e3fff.png] 

To establish the **symbolic form** of congruence, we match vertices based on the given side lengths:

⇒ Given AB = EF, the vertices A and B correspond to E and F.

⇒ Given BC = DF, the vertices B and C correspond to F and D.

⇒ Looking at both, the **common vertex** B in the first triangle matches the **common vertex** F in the second triangle ⇒ B ↔ F.

⇒ From BC = DF and B ↔ F, it follows that C ↔ D.

⇒ From AB = EF and B ↔ F, it follows that A ↔ E.

⇒ Therefore, vertex C matches D, vertex B matches F, and vertex A matches E.

⇒ Writing this in order: ΔCBA is congruent to ΔDFE.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔCBA ≅ ΔDFE.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

SSS Congruence Criterion

If three sides of one triangle are equal to the three sides of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent by SSS rule.

CPCT (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles)

Once two triangles are proven congruent, their corresponding angles and remaining sides are automatically equal.

Congruence Naming Convention

The order of vertices in a congruence statement must strictly follow the correspondence of equal sides and equal angles.</p

questions.question: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF with BC : EF = 1 : 4. Find the area(Δ DEF) : area(ΔABC).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **similar triangles**, the **ratio of their areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Given side ratio **BC : EF = 1 : 4**.

⇒ Area(ΔABC) : Area(ΔDEF) = 1² : 4² = 1 : 16.

⇒ Area(ΔDEF) : Area(ΔABC) = **16 : 1**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **ΔABC ∼ ΔDEF**

⇒ Ratio of sides **BC : EF = 1 : 4**

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = (BC ÷ EF)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3199c69e49572c0acd01a9021c529651a018f860f9ba70145a5c1e88ff1b6b2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ According to the **Area Theorem** of **similar triangles**:

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = (BC)² ÷ (EF)²

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = (1)² ÷ (4)²

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = 1 ÷ 16

⇒ Area(ΔABC) : Area(ΔDEF) = 1 : 16

⇒ Inverting the ratio to find **Area(ΔDEF) : Area(ΔABC)**:

⇒ Area(ΔDEF) : Area(ΔABC) = 16 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Similar Triangles Area Theorem

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides, altitudes, or medians.

Perimeter Ratio

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides (linear ratio).

SAS Similarity

Two triangles are similar if two sides of one triangle are proportional to two sides of another triangle and their included angles are equal.</p

questions.question: The corresponding sides of two similar triangles are in the ratio of 2: 3. If the area of the smaller triangle is 36 sq cm, then the area of the bigger triangle is:

⇒ Area(Bigger) = 9 × 9

**__Additional Information__**

Area Ratio Theorem

For any two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, or perimeters.

Perimeter Ratio

The ratio of the **perimeters** of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P₁/P₂ = s₁/s₂.

questions.question: PN is a secant intersecting a circle at points M and N such that PN > PM. A tangent PT is drawn to the circle touching it at T. If PM = 32 cm and PT = 40 cm, what is the length (in cm) of the chord MN?
questions.solution:
* __Shortcut Trick__

According to the **Tangent-Secant Theorem**, when a tangent and a secant are drawn from an external point to a circle:

PT² = PM × PN

⇒ 40² = 32 × PN

⇒ 1600 = 32 × PN

⇒ PN = 50 cm

Chord MN = PN − PM = 50 − 32 = 18 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of tangent **PT** = 40 cm

Length of external part of secant **PM** = 32 cm

**Formula Used:**

For an external point P, if PT is a **tangent** and P-M-N is a **secant**, then PT² = PM × PN.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cd45fdfeb0881c203cfa74f20112ae8a15089ac92620dcbaff4f2837b407881.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the length of the chord **MN** be x* cm.

⇒ **PN** = **PM** + **MN**

⇒ **PN** = 32 + *x*

Using the theorem:

⇒ 40² = 32 × (32 + *x*)

⇒ 1600 = 32 × (32 + *x*)

⇒ 32 + *x* = 1600 ÷ 32

⇒ 32 + *x* = 50

⇒ *x* = 50 − 32

⇒ *x* = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment and a secant segment are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, then the square of the measure of the tangent segment is equal to the product of the measures of the secant segment and its external secant segment.

Intersecting Chords Theorem

If two chords intersect inside a circle, the product of the lengths of the segments of one chord is equal to the product of the lengths of the segments of the other chord: PA × PB = PC × PD.

Two Secants Theorem

If two secant segments are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, then the product of the measures of one secant segment and its external part is equal to the product of the measures of the other secant segment and its external part.</p

**Given:**

The ratio of the lengths of two corresponding sides of two similar triangles is 17 : 13.

**Formula Used:**

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

**Calculation:**

Let the ratio of the lengths of the corresponding sides be 17/13.

Ratio of areas of the triangles = (Ratio of the lengths of the sides)²

⇒ Ratio of areas = (17/13)²

⇒ Ratio of areas = 17² / 13²

⇒ Ratio of areas = 289 / 169

**The ratio of the areas of the two triangles is 289 : 169.**

questions.question: In ΔPQR and ΔXYZ, the given side lengths are PQ = 5 cm, QR = 6 cm, PR = 7 cm and XY = 5 cm, YZ = 6 cm, XZ = 7 cm. Which of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ΔPQR:

PQ = 5 cm, QR = 6 cm, PR = 7 cm

In ΔXYZ:

XY = 5 cm, YZ = 6 cm, XZ = 7 cm

**Formula used:**

SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence Rule:

If three sides of one triangle are equal to three sides of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent.

**Calculation:**

Comparing side lengths:

PQ = XY = 5 cm

QR = YZ = 6 cm

PR = XZ = 7 cm

Since all corresponding sides are equal, by the SSS Congruence Rule:

⇒ ΔPQR ≅ ΔXYZ

**∴ The correct statement is ΔPQR ≅ ΔXYZ.**

Polygon ABCDE with:

AE = 20 cm

AB = 15 cm

BCDE is a square

Using the Pythagorean theorem, since AE = 20 cm and AB = 15 cm,

15, 20 forms a Pythagorean triples

BE is the hypotenuse: BE² = AE² + AB²

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03b902ec87f2899ab4a8b3a1844d4b731fef4267f32ed29ef8a8919766c528b6.png]

questions.question: A pair of parallel lines is intersected by a transversal such that ∠1 and ∠2 form a pair of alternate interior angles. If m∠1 = 75°, what is the measure of m∠2?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a pair of **parallel lines** is intersected by a **transversal**, the **alternate interior angles** are always equal.

Given: m∠1 = 75°

Since ∠1 and ∠2 are a pair of alternate interior angles, m∠2 = m∠1.

⇒ m∠2 = 75°

**∴ The correct answer is 75°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lines **L₁** and **L₂** are parallel (L₁ || L₂).

Transversal **T** intersects these lines.

Measure of angle 1 (m∠1) = 75°

∠1 and ∠2 are **alternate interior angles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c342f6668fdc69671ac12c5cc4e247e4bd8d9c3ccdae2b3fd34af73b68f6d929.png] 

**Property Used:**

If two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the **Alternate Interior Angles Theorem** states that the resulting alternate interior angles are congruent (equal in measure).

**Calculations:**

⇒ m∠1 = m∠2 (By Alternate Interior Angles Theorem)

⇒ 75° = m∠2

⇒ m∠2 = 75°

**∴ The correct answer is 75°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. For parallel lines, these are always **equal**.

Consecutive Interior Angles

Pairs of angles on one side of the transversal and between the two parallel lines. They are **supplementary**, meaning their sum is **180°**.

Alternate Exterior Angles

Pairs of angles on opposite sides of the transversal and outside the two parallel lines. For parallel lines, these are also **equal**.</p

questions.question: A pair of parallel lines is intersected by a transversal such that ∠1 and ∠2 form a pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal. If m∠1 = 65°, what is the measure of ∠2?

Alternate Interior Angles

When parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, alternate interior angles are equal in measure.

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others are equal if the lines are parallel.

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other at the vertex are always equal.</p

questions.question: The difference in the measures of two complementary angles is 18°. Find the measure of the smaller angle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two angles whose **sum** (S) and **difference** (D) are known:

**Smaller angle** = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2

Sum of **complementary angles** = 90° | Difference = 18°

Smaller angle = (90° − 18°) ÷ 2 = 72° ÷ 2 = 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two angles are **complementary**.

Difference between them = 18°.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of two **complementary angles** = 90°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf472bf6e6c6f40ebb545420ea157766db30875edfd3a647ca122ddc61d7beda.png] 

Let the two angles be **x** and **y**, where **x** is the smaller angle.

⇒ y + x = 90° --- (Equation 1)

⇒ y − x = 18° --- (Equation 2)

Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ (y + x) − (y − x) = 90° − 18°

⇒ 2x = 72°

⇒ x = 72° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 36°

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

Two angles are called complementary if their sum is exactly 90°.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are called supplementary if their sum is exactly 180°.

Linear Pair

Adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines that sum to 180° are known as a linear pair.</p

questions.question: A pair of parallel lines is intersected by a transversal such that ∠1 and ∠2 form a pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal. If m ∠1 = 125°, what is the measure of ∠2?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. If the lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal. These angles are always equal when lines are parallel.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles whose measures sum up to 180° are called supplementary angles.</p

questions.question: If a pair of linear equations is consistent, then the lines will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A **consistent** system of equations means there is **at least one solution**.

**Intersecting lines** provide exactly **one solution** (unique).

**Coincident lines** provide **infinitely many solutions**.

Since both cases yield solutions, a consistent pair must be **intersecting or coincident**.

**∴ The correct answer is intersecting or coincident.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A pair of linear equations is **consistent**.

Consider the general form: a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0.

A system is **consistent** if it has **one or more solutions**.

⇒ Case 1: **Unique Solution** (Intersecting Lines)

⇒ Condition: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂

⇒ Case 2: **Infinite Solutions** (Coincident Lines)

⇒ Condition: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

⇒ If the system is **inconsistent**, it has **no solution** (Parallel Lines).

⇒ Condition: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

**∴ The correct answer is intersecting or coincident.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inconsistent System

A pair of linear equations with no solution is called **inconsistent**, representing **parallel lines**.

Dependent Equations

A pair of **dependent** linear equations is always **consistent** and has infinitely many solutions (coincident lines).</p

questions.question: If the angles (5x - 2)° and 82° form a pair of supplementary angles, then the value of x is:

For **supplementary angles**, the sum is always 180°.

(5x − 2) + 82 = 180

5x + 80 = 180

5x = 100

x = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First angle = (5x − 2)°

Second angle = 82°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of **supplementary angles** = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/141a9a0abc05d2f14b979755015e2e339138aed03b6d2c270d15a5d4077c368a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (5x − 2) + 82 = 180

⇒ 5x + 80 = 180

⇒ 5x = 180 − 80

⇒ 5x = 100

⇒ x = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 20

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are called supplementary when their measures add up to 180 degrees. They form a linear pair if they are adjacent.

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if the sum of their measures is exactly 90 degrees.

Linear Pair Postulate

If two angles form a linear pair, then the angles are supplementary, meaning they lie on a straight line.</p

questions.question: If AB = k + 3, BC = 2k and AC = 4k - 5, then for what value of ‘k’ does B lie on AC?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **Point B** to lie on the line segment **AC**, the sum of segments **AB** and **BC** must be exactly equal to **AC**.

AB + BC = AC

(k + 3) + (2k) = 4k − 5

3k + 3 = 4k − 5

k = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **AB** = k + 3

Length of **BC** = 2k

Length of **AC** = 4k − 5

**Property used:**

If three points **A, B, and C** are **collinear** and **B** lies between **A** and **C**, then by the **Segment Addition Postulate**, the total distance **AC** is the sum of the parts **AB** and **BC**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c50dc19ecad1c7ede4c87f8dc45f25578772178206424d9c45ccb3bda330fa4a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ AB + BC = AC

⇒ (k + 3) + 2k = 4k − 5

⇒ 3k + 3 = 4k − 5

⇒ 3 + 5 = 4k − 3k

⇒ 8 = k

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Collinearity of Points

Three points are collinear if they lie on the same straight line. For points A, B, and C, if AB + BC = AC, then B lies between A and C.

Triangle Inequality Theorem

In any triangle, the sum of any two sides must be greater than the third side (AB + BC > AC). If AB + BC = AC, the "triangle" degenerates into a straight line.

Distance Formula

In coordinate geometry, the distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²).</p

questions.question: What is the measure of each exterior angle of a regular decagon?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **regular polygon**, the sum of all **exterior angles** is always 360°.

A **decagon** has **n = 10** sides.

Each exterior angle = 360° ÷ n = 360° ÷ 10 = 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Shape = **Regular Decagon**.

**Formula Used:** Each Exterior Angle of a regular polygon = 360° ÷ n, where n is the number of sides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a2b72e1261369c8a63c48343eccdefc3b8f9544fd31dcbe167743db8bd0cdf4.png] 

⇒ Number of sides in a **decagon** (n) = 10.

⇒ Sum of all exterior angles of any **convex polygon** = 360°.

⇒ Since the polygon is **regular**, all exterior angles are equal.

⇒ Each exterior angle = 360° ÷ 10.

⇒ Each exterior angle = 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Interior Angle of a Regular Polygon

Each interior angle is given by [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n. For a decagon, it is [(10 − 2) × 180°] ÷ 10 = 144°.

Relation between Interior and Exterior Angles

The sum of an **interior angle** and its corresponding **exterior angle** is always 180° (linear pair).

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n − 2) × 180°.</p

questions.question: When three parallel lines are cut by two transversals and the intercepts made by the first transversal are in the ratio 3 : 5, then the intercepts made by the second transversal are in the ratio ____
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the **Intercept Theorem** (also known as Thales' Theorem for parallel lines), the ratio of **intercepts** made by any transversal on a set of **parallel lines** is always **constant**.

If the first transversal makes intercepts in the ratio 3 : 5, every other transversal will also make intercepts in the same ratio 3 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three **parallel lines** (say l₁, l₂, l₃) and two **transversals** (say t₁ and t₂). The intercepts made by t₁ are in ratio 3 : 5.

**Formula Used:** If three or more **parallel lines** are cut by two **transversals**, then the segments intercepted on the transversals are **proportional**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed2381b427577ebb1eda5e893e1ab549c53a14b41deff5c184c6dcebe9390099.png] 

⇒ Let the intercepts on the first transversal be **A** and **B**. Ratio A : B = 3 : 5.

⇒ Let the corresponding intercepts on the second transversal be **C** and **D**.

⇒ According to the **proportionality theorem**: A ÷ B = C ÷ D

⇒ 3 ÷ 5 = C ÷ D

⇒ C : D = 3 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Intercept Theorem

If three or more **parallel lines** intersect two transversals, then they cut off the transversals in **proportional segments**.

Midpoint Theorem

A special case of this theorem where the ratio is **1 : 1**, implying the **parallel line** passes through the **midpoints** of the transversal segments.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT)

Also known as **Thales's Theorem**, it states that if a line is drawn **parallel** to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides, the other two sides are divided in the same **ratio**.</p

questions.question: Find the number of sides in a regular polygon if its each interior angle is 165°.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Each **exterior angle** = 180° − 165° = 15°.

Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ **Exterior Angle**.

⇒ n = 360° ÷ 15° = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Each interior angle of a **regular polygon** = 165°.

**Formula Used:** Interior angle of a regular polygon = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n, where **n** is the number of sides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c4a50899bdcc9f58aac38d16f5b2a3e4bf4ea56cb8091f2c10b80e7af206161.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 165° = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

⇒ 165n = 180n − 360

⇒ 180n − 165n = 360

⇒ 15n = 360

⇒ n = 360 ÷ 15

⇒ n = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all **interior angles** of a polygon with n sides is always (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon, the sum of all **exterior angles** (one at each vertex) is always 360°.

Regular Polygon Property

In a **regular polygon**, all sides and all interior angles are equal. The **exterior angle** = 360° ÷ n.</p

questions.question: If a regular polygon has 20 diagonals, then the sum of its interior angles is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of **diagonals** = n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 20

⇒ n(n − 3) = 40

⇒ By observation, 8 × 5 = 40, so **n = 8** (Octagon).

⇒ **Sum of interior angles** = (n − 2) × 180°

⇒ (8 − 2) × 180° = 6 × 180° = 1080°.

**∴ The correct answer is 1080°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number of diagonals = 20

**Formula Used:**

1. Number of diagonals in an **n-sided polygon** = [n(n − 3)] / 2

2. Sum of **interior angles** = (n − 2) × 180°

**Calculations:**

⇒ [n(n − 3)] / 2 = 20

⇒ n² − 3n = 40

⇒ n² − 3n − 40 = 0

⇒ n² − 8n + 5n − 40 = 0

⇒ n(n − 8) + 5(n − 8) = 0

⇒ (n − 8)(n + 5) = 0

⇒ Since **n** (number of sides) cannot be negative, **n = 8**.

⇒ Sum of interior angles = (8 − 2) × 180°

⇒ 6 × 180° = 1080°.

**∴ The correct answer is 1080°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon, the sum of all **exterior angles** is always constant and equal to 360°.

Individual Interior Angle

In a **regular polygon**, each interior angle is calculated as [(n − 2) × 180°] / n.

Relation between Angles

At any vertex of a polygon, the **Interior Angle + Exterior Angle = 180°**.</p

⇒ Angle = 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all **interior angles** of a polygon with n sides is (n − 2) × 180°.</p
